stem: While coordinating hepatopulmonary syndrome (HPS) evaluation for a liver transplant candidate, which diagnostic study aligns with standard references?

options.text: Standing and supine arterial blood gas analyses on room air and with 100% oxygen
Isolated serum amylase measurement without pulmonary testing
Routine bone marrow biopsy before any pulmonary assessment
HPS evaluation requires no arterial blood gas testing

explanation.rationale_correct: HPS evaluation includes standing and supine arterial blood gas analyses performed on room air and with 100% oxygen, along with studies such as macroaggregated albumin scan and bubble echocardiography when indicated.

rationale_incorrect.B: HPS evaluation focuses on pulmonary gas exchange and shunt assessment rather than isolated amylase testing.
rationale_incorrect.C: Bone marrow biopsy is not part of standard HPS evaluation protocols.
rationale_incorrect.D: Arterial blood gas analyses are specifically listed in HPS evaluation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 1, Evaluation → Liver transplantation → Additional evaluation → 4.b.ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: evaluation for HPS includes … Standing and supine arterial blood gas analyses are performed on room air and with 100% oxygen

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → Liver transplantation → Additional evaluation → 4.b.ii. (HPS evaluation with arterial blood gas analyses); PDF p. 44 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. HPS diagnostic-evaluation angle distinct from liver MELD waitlist removal (cctc-2044) and cardiac stress testing (cctc-2028); anchor verified on Cupples p. 44.

stem: When reviewing immunosuppression options for a kidney transplant candidate, which requirement applies to belatacept use per standard references?

options.text: The recipient must be seropositive for Epstein-Barr virus IgG to decrease PTLD risk
Belatacept may be used only in Epstein-Barr virus–seronegative recipients
Belatacept requires daily therapeutic drug level monitoring like calcineurin inhibitors
Belatacept eliminates the need for any maintenance immunosuppression

explanation.rationale_correct: The transplant recipient must be seropositive for Epstein-Barr virus IgG to decrease the risk of developing posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease when using belatacept.

rationale_incorrect.B: EBV IgG seropositivity is required, not seronegativity, because PTLD risk is higher with EBV-seronegative recipients on belatacept.
rationale_incorrect.C: Belatacept does not require therapeutic drug level monitoring.
rationale_incorrect.D: Belatacept is used as part of maintenance immunosuppression rather than replacing all immunosuppressive therapy.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: transplant recipient must be seropositive for Epstein-Barr virus IgG to decrease the risk of developing PTLD

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 4 → Belatacept → 3.c. (recipient must be seropositive for Epstein-Barr virus IgG to decrease PTLD risk); PDF p. 157 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

stem: A lung waitlist candidate is placed on inactive status while temporarily unsuitable for transplant. According to OPTN Policy 3.6.A, how does waiting time accrue during inactivity?

options.text: Unlimited waiting time accrues while the candidate remains inactive
No waiting time accrues while the candidate remains inactive
Waiting time accrues only for the first 30 cumulative inactive days
Waiting time accrues only when the candidate is younger than 18 years

explanation.rationale_correct: OPTN Table 3-3 specifies that lung candidates accrue unlimited waiting time while inactive, similar to kidney candidates and unlike heart or liver candidates who accrue no inactive waiting time.

rationale_incorrect.B: No inactive accrual applies to heart and liver candidates, not lung candidates.
rationale_incorrect.C: A 30-day cumulative inactive accrual limit applies to intestine candidates, not lung candidates.
rationale_incorrect.D: Lung inactive waiting-time rules are not limited to pediatric candidates.

primary_anchor.section: Policy 3.6.A → Table 3-3 Waiting Time for Inactive Candidates → Lung
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Lung … Unlimited time … Candidates accrue waiting time while inactive

references.locator: Policy 3.6.A → Table 3-3: Waiting Time for Inactive Candidates (lung candidates accrue unlimited waiting time while inactive); PDF p. 46 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Lung inactive waiting-time angle paired with heart no-accrual (cctc-2045) and kidney unlimited accrual (cctc-2037); anchor verified on optn-policies p. 46.

stem: When communicating the transplant team's recommendation to a liver candidate with hepatopulmonary syndrome, which counseling point aligns with standard evaluation references?

options.text: Hepatopulmonary syndrome is reversible with transplantation and is not a contraindication to liver transplant
Hepatopulmonary syndrome permanently prohibits listing for any transplantation
Hepatorenal syndrome alone mandates isolated kidney transplantation instead of liver transplant
Pulmonary complications of liver failure never improve after transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Both hepatopulmonary syndrome and hepatorenal syndrome are reversible with transplantation and are not contraindications to liver transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: HPS is an indication for evaluation and transplant rather than a permanent contraindication.
rationale_incorrect.C: Hepatorenal syndrome in the setting of liver failure is addressed through liver transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.D: HPS and HRS are described as reversible with transplantation rather than permanently unimproved.
